sections.COMMENTS:
This composite source straddles the Livorno Hills, a few km SE of the city of Livorno. This source is a ENE-dipping, normal fault parallel to the NNW-SSE trending Tyrrhenian margin of the Tuscany region.
Historical catalogues (Boschi et al., 2000; Gruppo di Lavoro CPTI, 2004; Guidoboni et al., 2007) show sparse intermediate to damaging earthquakes in the area. In particular, this region has been affected by the 14 August 1846 (Mw 5.7, Orciano Pisano), and the 1 April 1950 (Mw 5.1, Rosignano Marittima) earthquakes.
This Source is based on the recent tectonic activity of the western sector of the inner Northern Apennines, and on the occurrence of the 14 August 1846 earthquake. In particular, this Source belongs to the normal fault system that borders the NW-SE trending horst and graben that developed during the late Miocene-Pleistocene (e.g. Carmignani et al., 1994, 2001).
The main segment of this Source has been associated with the 14 August 1846 earthquake. For an in-depth analysis of seismogenesis in this region, the reader can refer to the Individual Source in this Database.
The strike of the source is based on geomorphological evidence. The dip is based on geological and geomorphological evidence. The rake, indicative of pure normal faulting, is based on geodynamic considerations. Minimum and maximum depth is deduced from the geological context. Slip rate was inferred from geological observations in other structures that share the same tectonic regime with this Source.

pictures.c: Geochemical signature of Plio-Quaternary basins of the Northern Apennines. In the Val di Fine basin the He3/He4 ratio is in the range 0.14-0.16. This ratio is very sensitive to deep fluids rising from the mantle (from Minissale et al. [2000]).
